The correct strategy is to strictly map "above" to a lower rank number (1st is above 2nd) and "below" to a higher rank number (2nd is below 1st) immediately upon reading the clues. I will calculate the exact integer values for each person step-by-step before selecting the option for who finished second.

New plan: I failed because I made a critical arithmetic error in the final step of the deduction. I correctly identified that Rob must be in slot 7 (since he is below Mya at 2nd, and slots 3-6 were taken), but I incorrectly concluded that Ana must be in slot 1 without verifying if slot 1 was actually available or if I had miscounted the remaining slots. Specifically, I listed "Remaining Slots: 1, 4, 5, 7" but then assigned Rob to 7 and Ana to 1 without explicitly confirming that no other constraints blocked Ana from slot 1. The error was skipping the explicit verification of the "only person left" logic for the final empty slot. Next time, I will strictly list the set of available slots, assign every person to a specific slot based on constraints, and then explicitly state "The only remaining person is X, and the only remaining slot is Y" before finalizing the order. I will also double-check that "second-to-last" in a 7-person race is indeed 6th, not 5th, to ensure the initial fixed points are correct.
